localPatches.summary: An opt-in resolver mode owns original soundtrack Inputs independently from picture proxies, with combined descriptor identity, reuse and cleanup. Defaults and original-media export remain unchanged.
The pre-1.1 Dojo command wire schema remains at @dojo-video-engine/schema/commands while current traffic migrates to upstream @dojo-video-engine/commands.
Relative NodeNext .js import suffixes are removed mechanically because Next/Webpack compiles the vendored TypeScript sources directly; package imports and runtime behavior are unchanged.
The shared export frame loop owns bounded scratch and static caches across frames, disposing only resources it created.
Preview audio prefetches one successor and schedules AudioContext boundaries while preserving seek cancellation and bounded memory.
An optional cancellable host frame renderer lets compatible silent previews render in a worker without opening duplicate main-thread media.
Trusted internal rendering reuses evaluated frames and bounded exact text metrics, invalidating font-dependent widths/rasters when resources change.
Export reuses audio placement plans, bounded sample copies and one-chunk lookahead when audio/video media Inputs are independent.
Asset preparation caps actual resource creators at four and consumes policy-bounded responses as native Blobs without whole-file JavaScript buffer copies.

Ranged audio decoding warms up at most 100 ms before a trim/chunk boundary to restore compressed-codec overlap state, while copying only the exact requested PCM window and preserving cancellation and cache budgets.

Audio envelope interpolation blocks stop at keyframe sample boundaries, preserving exact piecewise-linear gains at integer/fractional knots and chunk offsets without increasing the 128-sample maximum or allocating a boundary list.

Measures the actual AAC encoder profile using bounded synthetic audio, then repairs only MP4 presentation/tail metadata before Blob verification or stream close. Encoded media bytes remain unchanged and file rollback stays owned by the original writer.
